subject.title: feat(gateway): include produced messageId on chat final/aborted events

question: Should Gateway terminal events expose the persisted transcript row ID as the stable public produced-message identifier, or should OpenClaw provide a separate opaque run-to-message reference?
rationale: The patch is additive and proven, but it promotes an internal persistence identifier into a client contract that future storage and migration work must preserve.

options.title: Adopt transcript IDs as the Gateway contract
options.body: Merge the additive field and treat `messageId` as a stable client-facing identifier with compatibility obligations for future transcript changes.

options.title: Use an opaque produced-message reference
options.body: Ask for a narrow redesign that keeps transcript storage IDs private while giving clients a stable lookup or opaque identifier.

options.title: Pause the feature direction
options.body: Defer the new event field until Gateway ownership defines the intended external message-identity contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt transcript IDs as the Gateway contract
recommendation.body: Merge the additive field and treat `messageId` as a stable client-facing identifier with compatibility obligations for future transcript changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor has the most direct evidence for the implementation paths, though a repository Gateway owner should make the final contract decision.
